workflow: Mortgage lender underwriting help-desk / scenario-desk log, US agency lending (Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, FHA, VA, USDA). Loan officers, processors and line underwriters submit guideline questions about a specific file or a hypothetical scenario; a senior underwriter, underwriting manager or credit-policy owner answers; answers accumulate in email, chat and ticket queues. EVIDENCE LIMITATION, stated first: WebSearch was exhausted (200/200) before this analysis began and the egress proxy blocked every GSE, HUD, CFPB, MBA, vendor and press host. Everything below that is not from a GitHub- or npm-hosted artefact fetched in this session (CFPB HMDA platform LAR spec, the EBA Q&A mirror corpus, two third-party Encompass API connectors, one lender-published SDK, two open-source underwriting rule engines) is labelled [RECALL, unverified] or estimate. No help-desk volume, repeat rate, cost per question or manual-underwrite share was measured anywhere in this exercise; the walkthrough is structural, not quantitative, and recall is never presented as measurement.
geography: United States first: agency lending is a US-specific structure in which two GSEs and three federal agencies publish the operative underwriting guides and run the automated underwriting systems (DU, LPA, TOTAL Scorecard, GUS) that execute them; the HMDA public LAR spec fetched from the CFPB repo enumerates exactly these four AUS names plus Other and Not applicable (fields 96 to 101). EU and France have no GSE analogue: the bank's own credit policy is the operative rule under EBA GL/2020/06 and the Mortgage Credit Directive, so the ownership objection is weaker there, but the EU AI Act, GDPR Article 22 and, in France, the HCSF exception quota constrain automation more heavily. Differences are treated in the regulatory section.
triggering_event: A file or pre-application scenario presents facts the guide addresses only partly: a borrower with 18 months of self-employment history in a business that changed entity type; rental income from a departing residence with a lease signed after application; a large deposit whose source is a gift from a relative through a third-party account; a condo project with pending litigation; a non-arm's-length purchase from an employer; a gap in employment across a Refer/Eligible DU finding on an FHA file. The loan officer or processor cannot tell whether the file is eligible or how to calculate qualifying income, or wants to know whether the lender will accept something the guide permits but the lender's overlay matrix is silent on. The question is submitted to the scenario desk (email alias, Teams channel, ticket queue, or a field in the LOS) before or during underwriting. Basis: [RECALL, unverified] of industry practice; the finder and verifier in the banking cluster recorded the same structure and could not source a volume.
available_rules: Layered and versioned by external owners. (1) Fannie Mae Selling Guide and Freddie Mac Seller/Servicer Guide, with Selling Guide announcements roughly monthly and Freddie Mac Guide Bulletins on the order of 15 to 25 per year [RECALL, unverified; selling-guide.fanniemae.com and guide.freddiemac.com blocked]. (2) HUD Handbook 4000.1 for FHA, VA Lenders Handbook, USDA HB-1-3555 [RECALL, blocked]. (3) The executable form of those guides: DU, LPA, TOTAL Scorecard, GUS, whose result codes (Approve/Eligible, Approve/Ineligible, Refer/Eligible, Refer/Ineligible, Refer with Caution, Accept, Caution, Out of Scope) are enumerated in the fetched HMDA LAR spec, fields 102 to 107 (government open-source repo). (4) Lender overlays and product matrices: minimum FICO, maximum DTI, reserves, occupancy and property-type restrictions, encoded in LOS business rules and product-and-pricing engines. The open-source LoanScope engine fetched this session models exactly this layer as declarative ProgramRules with override-wins merging of lender tiers onto agency base constraints and 18 first-class eligibility checks (LTV, CLTV, DTI, FICO, loan amount, reserves, cash-to-close, occupancy, purpose, property type, units, borrower restrictions, state restrictions, cash-out, buydown, MI, AUS, appraisal); its own README says these rules otherwise 'get hand-coded into spreadsheets and one-off scripts'. (5) Investor and mortgage-insurer guidelines for non-delegated or MI-insured files. (6) Federal law: Regulation Z ability-to-repay verification standards, Regulation B adverse-action reasons, fair-lending examination expectations on documented and consistent exceptions [RECALL, unverified]. The rules constrain but do not fully determine income calculation methods, acceptability of unusual documentation, and edge-case eligibility; the guide owner, not the lender, holds the binding reading.
available_facts: Structured and mostly obtainable. The application (URLA/ULAD) and the LOS carry loan type (Conventional, FHA, VA, USDA), purpose, occupancy, property type, loan amount, interest rate, credit score, annual income, employer, milestones and a conditions list with status, category and responsibility; the fetched Encompass v3 connector spec exposes loans, milestones, conditions, documents, rate locks and pipeline endpoints, and the lender-published Royal United Mortgage SDK wraps the same Encompass API alongside Optimal Blue (pricing) and payroll vendors. Income documentation (pay stubs, W-2s, tax returns, bank statements), the AUS finding, the appraisal and the credit report are on file or requested as conditions. Facts that are often missing at the time of the question: the actual documents behind a hypothetical, the exact wording of a lease or gift letter, the condo questionnaire, verification of employment. HMDA denial-reason codes (fetched spec, field 68: DTI, employment history, credit history, collateral, insufficient cash, unverifiable information, incomplete application, MI denied, other) show that the lender-reported reasons for adverse outcomes are fact and eligibility categories; there is no code for guideline ambiguity.
why_it_escalates: Four distinct reasons that must not be conflated. (a) Missing evidence: the asker wants to know what documents would make the file work (category A). (b) Factual classification: is this income stable, is this a large deposit, is this a primary residence (B). (c) Guide meaning: how the Selling Guide or 4000.1 treats a fact pattern the text addresses imprecisely, for example how to average declining self-employment income or whether a particular asset type counts as reserves (C). (d) Lender policy: whether the lender will accept a file the guide permits, or how an overlay applies to an unlisted case (E for the risk-appetite decision, H when the same question about the lender's own overlay recurs). Escalation happens because line staff lack authority to bind the lender to a reading that carries rep-and-warrant exposure; a wrong reading on an agency file is a repurchase or indemnification risk discovered in post-close QC or GSE review [RECALL]. The verifier's structural point stands: for reason (c), the lender's senior underwriter settles nothing authoritatively, because the GSE or FHA can overturn the reading on QC review; the settlement is a risk position. Only reason (d) is a genuine authoritative settlement, and the verifier's prior, unrefuted here, is that (d) is a minority of desk traffic.
who_resolves: File-level answers: senior underwriter or underwriting manager (authority tiers by loan amount and product are standard [RECALL]). Policy-level answers: credit-policy manager, Chief Credit Officer or a credit-policy committee, who alone can create or amend an overlay. Guide meaning: the GSE account team, Fannie Mae Ask Poli, Freddie Mac seller support, or the FHA Resource Center, whose answers bind only when they reach the published guide or an announcement [RECALL, blocked]. Investor or MI company for non-delegated or insured files. FHA Refer files and specified credit histories must be manually underwritten by a DE underwriter applying compensating-factor tables regardless of any internal precedent [RECALL, 4000.1 blocked]. There is therefore a clear internal owner for the lender's own policy and no internal owner for the largest interpretive area.
what_gets_settled: Three different objects. (1) A per-file answer ('this file is eligible if you document X'), which is a condition on the loan record in the LOS, not a rule. (2) A lender-policy clarification ('we do not accept asset depletion income on second homes'; 'departing-residence rental income requires a 12-month lease and first-month receipt'), which is an overlay change or a product-matrix edit, effective-dated and pushed into LOS business rules and the PPE. (3) A reading of the agency guide ('we treat a two-year average as required when the most recent year declines'), which the lender records as a training note or FAQ but which remains the GSE's to confirm; the owner is also encoding this area itself: Fannie Mae's Income Calculator for self-employment income with rep-and-warrant relief when used through DU, and Freddie Mac AIM [RECALL, unverified; flagged by the verifier as the strongest H3/H6 fact in the cluster if confirmed]. Only object (2) matches brief step 4 (authoritative settlement).
prospective: Split verdict. Object (2), lender-own-policy clarifications, apply prospectively by construction: an overlay edit binds every later file until the next policy revision, and the LOS and PPE already execute it. Object (3), agency-guide readings, are prospective only until the next guide release and are never authoritative; the GSE can reverse them on any file. Evidence is structural: LoanScope's declarative override-wins ProgramRules show how lender layers are applied prospectively over agency base rules in code (fetched open-source project); the Encompass connectors show conditions as per-file objects, not reusable rules (fetched third-party connectors, weak). The regulator-side analogue that could be measured, the EBA Single Rulebook Q&A corpus, confirms that owner-published interpretations are prospective and versioned, and also how slow and sparse they are: 103 of 2,166 final Q&As mention mortgages, 43 of them under credit risk, median 317 days from submission to final answer (computed from the fetched mirror; regulator corpus via third-party GitHub mirror). No lender-internal artefact demonstrating prospective application could be fetched.
recurrence: Unknown; not measured by anyone in this exercise. What can be said: the fact classes named above (self-employed and variable income, rental income, gifts and large deposits, condo eligibility, non-arm's-length transactions, employment gaps) recur across files at every lender because they are the standing hard cases of the guides [RECALL], and guide changes arrive roughly monthly [RECALL], which resets some settlements. Two sourced analogues bracket the rate at the owner level, both small: the EBA corpus adds about eight mortgage-related Q&As per year across the whole EU banking sector (103 over 2013 to 2026, computed from the fetched mirror), and the prior IPSA evidence found repetition plentiful at the level owners already govern with bright lines and scarce where disputes arise. The verifier's re-estimate of category H at 3 to 7 percent of underwriting questions, and only over the lender's own policy, is an estimate with no measurement behind it; this analysis found nothing to move it. A single lender's twelve-month desk log would settle the question in two weeks and is the only way to get the number.
current_systems: Executable guides: DU, LPA, TOTAL Scorecard, GUS (enumerated in the fetched HMDA LAR spec). LOS: ICE Encompass with business rules, conditions, milestones, field locks and templates (fetched connector READMEs list loans, milestones, conditions with status/category/responsibility, documents, rate locks, pipeline; the Activepieces piece lists field-lock management and template application); Blend, MeridianLink and others [RECALL]. Product-and-pricing engines (Optimal Blue appears in the fetched lender SDK; Polly [RECALL]). Overlay and product matrices in spreadsheets and PPE rules. Scenario-desk channels: email aliases, Teams or Slack channels, ticket tools, occasionally an LOS custom field [RECALL]. Guideline search and LLM guideline assistants sold to underwriters [RECALL, vendors blocked]. QC platforms (ACES) and GSE loan-quality tools [RECALL, blocked]. Owner-side encoders: Fannie Mae Income Calculator and Freddie Mac AIM [RECALL]. Open-source rule encoders exist as independent projects (LoanScope, mortctl; fetched), evidence that the guide-to-rule encoding problem attracts builders, not that settlement capture does.
minimal_product: WOULD DO: (1) Intake a scenario question with typed facts (product, purpose, occupancy, income type, document type, AUS finding, cited guide section) instead of free text. (2) Match the question against a ledger of prior settlements and return the standing answer with its owner, date, version and the guide version it was made under. (3) Route unmatched questions to the credit-policy owner and record the answer as one of two typed objects: an authoritative lender-policy settlement (effective-dated, prospective, exportable to Encompass business rules and the PPE as an overlay change) or a non-authoritative guide reading (a risk position with citation, expiring on the next release of the cited section). (4) Diff each monthly Selling Guide announcement, Guide Bulletin and 4000.1 revision against the ledger and flag settlements citing changed sections for re-ratification. (5) Produce the exception and interpretation register that fair-lending and QC reviewers ask for. WOULD NOT DO: underwrite files; replace or second-guess DU, LPA or TOTAL; decide FHA Refer or manually underwritten files, which a DE underwriter must decide by rule; approve exceptions or price them; write policy text; answer from guide text without a named owner's ratification; make any GSE guide reading binding, because the lender cannot. The honest description of the residual product is an overlay change-log with a question-matching front end, which is a feature of the LOS rules layer or of the guideline-assistant category, not a system of record.
buyer: Chief Credit Officer, SVP or VP of Underwriting, or credit-policy manager at an independent mortgage bank or a bank mortgage division; users are underwriting managers, scenario-desk staff, loan officers and processors. Budget sits in the LOS and underwriting technology line, where ICE (Encompass), pricing engines and guideline-assistant vendors already compete for it. Willingness to pay for a standalone settlement ledger is unknown; the finder and verifier both recorded it as unknown and nothing fetchable this session changes that.
roi_logic: All inputs are estimates unless labelled; the arithmetic is illustrative and should be replaced by customer-supplied figures. Take a mid-size IMB closing 10,000 agency loans a year (estimate). Assume 0.5 scenario or help-desk questions per closed loan, 5,000 questions a year (estimate; no lender publishes this). Assume 15 minutes of senior-underwriter or credit-policy time per answer at a fully loaded 75 dollars an hour (estimate; underwriter compensation figures were not fetchable): 1,250 hours, about 94,000 dollars a year of answering labour, plus asker waiting time that a search tool addresses as well as a ledger would. Category H, repeat questions about the lender's own policy that a standing settlement would answer deterministically, at the verifier's 3 to 7 percent re-estimate: 3,000 to 6,600 dollars a year of addressable labour; even at a generous 20 percent, 19,000 dollars. A lender ten times larger scales this to 30,000 to 190,000 dollars a year, still below the roughly 150,000 dollars of addressable labour needed to support a 50,000-dollar annual contract at a three-to-one value ratio except at the largest lenders under the generous assumption. Risk value does not rescue it: repurchase and indemnification losses are driven by income miscalculation and documentation defects found in QC [RECALL of QC defect taxonomies, blocked], and a lender-internal ledger of guide readings cannot make those readings correct in the GSE's eyes; the owner's own income calculator with rep-and-warrant relief [RECALL] addresses that risk more directly. Time-to-close value is real but is the pitch of guideline search and LLM assistants, which need no owner ratification and already sell into the same budget. Net: the economics support a feature inside the LOS rules layer or a guideline assistant, not standalone software.
review_split_A_to_H: Estimate only; no help-desk log was sampled and no primary source gives a reason breakdown. Basis: the structure of agency underwriting recalled by finder, verifier and this analyst; the HMDA denial-reason enumeration (fetched CFPB spec) as a weak external anchor showing that lender-reported adverse reasons are all fact and eligibility categories; the verifier's re-estimate of H at 3 to 7 percent, not contradicted by anything fetched. A missing evidence 30 to 40 percent (what to document, what the condition needs). B factual classification 15 to 20 percent (income stability, deposit source, occupancy). C interpretation of the agency guide 20 to 30 percent (income calculation methods, reserves, eligibility edge cases); this is the largest interpretive bucket and it is not settleable by the lender. D conflict of authorities 3 to 5 percent (guide versus investor, MI, state law). E discretion 5 to 10 percent (exception requests, compensating factors on manual underwrites, pricing exceptions). F commercial 2 to 5 percent (whether to take the file or price the exception). G one-off 3 to 5 percent. H repeatable ambiguity over the lender's own overlays and internal policy 3 to 10 percent. The kill threshold set by the verifier, that a clear majority of repeat questions must concern the lender's own policy, is judged unlikely to be met on this split, but that is a prior, not a measurement.

penalties_triggered: Existing rules engines already solve the codifiable part: overlays and product matrices live in LOS business rules and pricing engines, and the agency guides are executed by DU, LPA, TOTAL and GUS; the fetched LoanScope engine shows the lender layer is bright-line and declarative (severe; H3 and H6).

Humans must remain involved for legal or commercial reasons after precedent exists: FHA Refer and specified files require manual underwriting by a DE underwriter [RECALL]; Regulation Z ability-to-repay requires verified determination per file [RECALL]; the lender cannot make an agency-guide reading binding, so a human re-decides guide questions whenever the GSE or FHA may disagree (severe; brief step 4 fails for the largest interpretive bucket).

The main bottleneck is missing data rather than interpretation for an estimated 30 to 40 percent of desk questions, and the HMDA denial-reason codes are all fact and eligibility categories (moderate; H1, estimate).

Value per decision is too small: an answered question is worth minutes of senior-underwriter time, and the risk value sits with income and documentation defects the owner is encoding itself (moderate to severe).
Decisions are partly discretionary: exception requests, compensating factors and pricing exceptions are category E and F and stay per-loan (moderate).
Regulations constrain automation in the EU and France: AI Act high-risk obligations for creditworthiness assessment, GDPR Article 22, HCSF quota management (moderate, EU and France only).
Buyer is identifiable but budget sits in the LOS technology line where ICE and guideline-assistant vendors already compete, so a standalone ledger competes with a feature (moderate).

Not triggered: replacing a core system of record is not required, since Encompass exposes conditions, documents and pipeline through an API used by third parties and lenders themselves (fetched connectors and SDK); rules do change monthly and provenance and auditability do matter, which are positives that do not offset the penalties above.
regulatory_constraints_US_EU_FR: All items in this section are [RECALL, unverified] because every regulator and EU host was blocked. UNITED STATES: Regulation Z ability-to-repay (12 CFR 1026.43) requires the lender to consider and verify income, assets and debts using third-party records; the 2020 General QM rule replaced Appendix Q with a price-based test and allows lenders to verify using the standards in the Fannie Mae Selling Guide, Freddie Mac Guide and FHA, VA and USDA handbooks as of specified dates, which anchors the verification standard to the guide owners rather than to the lender's own readings. Regulation B and ECOA require specific adverse-action reasons and prohibit discouragement, and fair-lending examination procedures test whether underwriting exceptions are documented, consistently applied and tracked; this is the one regulatory pressure that favours a governed interpretation and exception register, but it is served today by exception-tracking reports and QC. FHA 4000.1 mandates manual underwriting for Refer files. GSE contracts allocate repurchase risk to the seller, which is why lender-side guide readings are risk positions. Automation of the deterministic parts is permitted and routine (AUS). EUROPEAN UNION: no GSE analogue; the bank's credit policy is the operative rule under EBA GL/2020/06, which requires documented, escalated and monitored deviations from credit policy and permits automated creditworthiness models with governance; the Mortgage Credit Directive (2014/17/EU, Article 18 and following) requires a thorough creditworthiness assessment per consumer; the EU AI Act Annex III 5(b) classifies creditworthiness assessment and credit scoring of natural persons as high-risk, with human oversight, logging and documentation obligations (application timing for high-risk systems has been subject to proposed deferral; treat as uncertain); GDPR Article 22 and the SCHUFA judgment (C-634/21) make scoring-driven decisions automated decisions with a right to human intervention. The EU picture therefore removes the ownership objection (the bank owns its policy) but adds a human-oversight floor, and the EBA Q&A corpus shows the regulator-level interpretive loop is small and slow (median 317 days, computed from the fetched mirror). FRANCE: the HCSF binding decision caps DSTI at 35 percent and maturity at 25 years with a 20 percent flexibility margin of quarterly production and sub-quotas; deviations are a rationed discretion budget counted against the margin, not an interpretation, so the highest-volume French mortgage exception class is category E by regulatory design. ACPR supervises algorithmic governance and explainability. A French deployment would be a quota-management and policy-deviation register, which core banking and origination systems already provide.
verdict: Weak evidence, leaning negative, for the lender-side underwriting help-desk as a standalone Sophon market; the workflow keeps its third-place ranking only because it is the one lending workflow whose historical log could be sampled cheaply. Structural findings hold after this session's additional research: the operative rules are owned, versioned and executed by the GSEs and FHA (AUS names and result codes are even enumerated in the CFPB HMDA spec), the lender layer is bright-line overlay policy that rules engines already encode (LoanScope demonstrates the shape in open source; Encompass exposes conditions and rules through an API that third parties and lenders themselves build on), the largest interpretive bucket is agency-guide meaning that the lender cannot settle authoritatively and that the owner is encoding itself, FHA Refer files require a human by rule, and the EU analogue of the owner-level loop (EBA Q&A) is real, prospective, tiny and slow. No volume, repeat rate or cost per question was measured by anyone, so H1 and H2 remain untested for this workflow; the ROI arithmetic on stated estimates yields low five figures of addressable labour at a mid-size lender, which supports a feature of the LOS rules layer or of a guideline assistant, not standalone software. Recommendation: do not build for this workflow; if any money is spent, spend two weeks classifying 300 to 500 questions from one lender's twelve-month help-desk log into the brief's eight categories, and continue only if categories 7 and 8 together exceed 25 percent of questions AND a clear majority of those concern the lender's own overlays or internal policy rather than the agency guide AND the settled classes recur at least ten times a year each; the prior from all evidence available here is that at least one of those three conditions fails. EVIDENCE LIMITATION restated: WebSearch exhausted, all regulator, GSE, vendor and press hosts blocked; sourced items are limited to GitHub- and npm-hosted artefacts; every other number is labelled recall or estimate and none of it is measurement.
